title: Bank Earnings Week Kicks Off (JPMorgan, UnitedHealth, Custodian Banks)
summary: Gotrade News - JPMorgan Chase (JPM) opens the third-quarter bank earnings season on Tuesday, October 13, with Wall Street expecting EPS of $5.86 on
body_markdown:
On credit, JPMorgan lowered its expected card net charge-off rate to about 3.2% from 3.4%, per Hudson Labs, which noted the second-quarter card net charge-off rate was 3.34%. Second-quarter average deposits rose 7% and average loans rose 10% from a year earlier, while expenses climbed 15%, the firm said.


Management has described its stance as "cautiously optimistic," and Hudson Labs flagged its views on macro risks, AI-driven productivity and deployment of more than $40 billion in excess capital as items to watch.


## Custodian Banks: State Street on Oct 14, BNY on Oct 15


The custodian banks follow later in the week. According to the company's own announcement,[State Street (STT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/stt/) will release third-quarter results at approximately 7:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, October 14, with a conference call at 11:00 a.m. ET.[BNY (BNY)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/bny/) plans to release its third-quarter results at approximately 6:30 a.m. ET on Thursday, October 15, followed by an 11:00 a.m. ET call, according to the bank's earnings calendar.


Date (ET) Scheduled reports, per the companies and Investing.com


Tuesday, Oct 13 JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Wells Fargo


Wednesday, Oct 14 State Street (about 7:30 a.m.), September CPI


Thursday, Oct 15 BNY (about 6:30 a.m.), producer prices, retail sales


## Nasdaq Futures Fall 0.8% Ahead of Bank Results


Late Monday, S&P 500 futures slipped 0.2% to 7,840.0 and Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.8% to 30,646.50, while Dow futures rose 0.2% to 52,187.0, according to Investing.com. On Monday, the Dow closed up 0.4%, the S&P 500 dipped 0.1% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.5%, the outlet reported.


Investing.com said the tech weakness tracked a sharp selloff in Asian memory chipmakers after reports that China's ChangXin Memory Technologies advanced a next-generation DRAM design.


Oil added another layer: Brent crude rose about 2% to $106.65 on Monday after strikes on Riyadh's international airport, and the outlet said higher oil could reinforce inflation pressures and complicate the Federal Reserve's outlook ahead of the[US CPI report this week](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/weekly-economic-outlook-2026-10-12/) .
